q: Does switching a boiler from coal to biomass qualify for carbon credits?
title: Coal to biomass boiler: carbon credits?
short: It can, but only as a registered project under an approved methodology, such as CDM AMS-I.C for renewable thermal energy, and only if the biomass counts as renewable, the switch is additional and leakage is deducted. Credits are earned on verified reductions after registration, not on past switches, and the net volume is usually well below the coal CO2 avoided.
audience: MSME owners in textiles, food and chemicals

ul: Methodology fit: AMS-I.C covers thermal energy from renewable sources for a user, for small projects up to 45 MW thermal. Larger projects need a large-scale methodology.
Renewable biomass: the fuel must meet the CDM definition of renewable biomass, for example crop residues or wood from sustainably managed sources.
Additionality: you must show the switch would not have happened anyway, for example because biomass was more costly or riskier than staying on coal.
Leakage: if the biomass would otherwise have been used by someone else who now burns fossil fuel, that effect is deducted.
Monitoring: fuel quantities, moisture and calorific values must be measured through the crediting period.

sections.h: Why the credit volume is lower than the coal avoided
p: Baseline emissions are worked out from the heat the boiler supplies, using the coal's emission factor and boiler efficiency. Project emissions include fossil fuel used to collect and transport biomass, any auxiliary fuel, and methane and nitrous oxide from biomass combustion. Leakage and any uncertainty discounts then come off. What is left is the creditable reduction.

Verra and Gold Standard each decide which methodologies and versions they accept, and their lists change. The ICVCM assesses categories for its Core Carbon Principles label, which affects price. In India, the offset mechanism under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme approves its own methodologies. Check the current list of each programme before you spend on a design document.

In your own inventory, CO2 from burning biomass is reported separately as biogenic CO2, outside Scope 1. Methane and nitrous oxide from biomass combustion stay in Scope 1. If you sell credits for the reduction, do not also claim it as an offset against your own target.

example.title: Labelled estimate: gross coal CO2 avoided
lines: Coal no longer burnt: 1,000 t a year = 1,000,000 kg
Factor: 2.42 kg CO2 per kg of coal (IPCC 2006 default)
Gross CO2 avoided: 1,000,000 x 2.42 = 2,420,000 kg = 2,420 t CO2 a year
Creditable reductions: 2,420 t less biomass transport fuel, auxiliary fuel, combustion methane and nitrous oxide, leakage and discounts
example.note: This is the upper bound before methodology deductions. The registered figure comes from the approved methodology and the verifier's report.

senseible: Senseible keeps your coal and biomass purchase invoices as a dated fuel-quantity record and shows carbon credit eligibility signals. It does not design projects, register them or issue credits; that runs through a standard and an accredited verifier.
